scope.scopeNotesMd: This report compares the local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions for the primitive datatype `id`. It treats the R6 file at the assigned path as the direct counterpart because the canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag all match the R4 artifact. Findings are limited to local `id` changes. Snapshot differences inherited from `Element`, `Extension`, or the base primitive infrastructure are documented as out of scope rather than counted as local findings.
outOfScope: Inherited `Element` constraint presentation changes visible in the `id` snapshot, including the `ele-1` human text change and removal of `xpath` fields, are base-artifact issues.
Inherited `Extension` content changes visible under `id.extension`, including definition wording/spelling and `ext-1` `xpath` removal, are not local `id` changes.
Any independent changes to the base `string` primitive or global primitive datatype hierarchy are out of scope except where the `id` StructureDefinition itself reports local metadata.
Profiles, implementation guides, examples, search parameters, operations, and application-specific uses of `id` are not assessed in this report.

narrativeReportMd:
# id R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard instance-breaking local changes were found for the `id` primitive datatype. R6 keeps the same canonical identity, element set, cardinalities, primitive regex `[A-Za-z0-9\-\.]{1,64}`, XML attribute representation for the value, and the same case-insensitive semantic description.

## Scope
This report covers the local `id` StructureDefinition in the R4 and R6 core packages. Inherited snapshot differences from `Element` and `Extension` are excluded by scope and should be assessed in those base-artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
The only local migration-relevant change found is a low-risk computable metadata correction: the R4 snapshot labels `id.value` with the `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension value `string`, while the R4 differential and R6 snapshot/differential label it `id`. This does not change the wire format or valid lexical space, but code generators or validators that rely only on snapshot annotations may observe a type-metadata change.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High findings. The sole local finding is Low impact and concerns generated tooling metadata rather than instance validity.

## Findings requiring human review
No finding requires human review. Confidence would improve with an official R4-to-R6 diff or rendered datatype narrative confirming the intended rationale for the snapshot metadata correction.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The local change appears justified because it aligns the R6 snapshot with the datatype identity and with the R4 differential. Keeping the R4 snapshot annotation as `string` would preserve a historical inconsistency rather than provide meaningful instance compatibility.

## Follow-up analysis
Base `Element` and `Extension` snapshot differences visible through `id` should be handled by their assigned reports.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard instance-breaking local `id` changes were found. The top migration concern is a Low-impact codegen/validator metadata correction for `id.value`; the top uncertainty is lack of an official diff or rendered narrative page explaining the change.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Existing R4 `id` values that satisfy the R4 regex remain valid under the R6 `id` definition, and valid R6 `id` values remain representable in R4. Migration work should focus on generated model or validator code that compares primitive fhir-type annotations from snapshots rather than on data transformation.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is High because the assigned R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions are present and have matching canonical identity, and the local differential for `id` is materially unchanged. Confidence is not absolute because no official diff, change note, or rendered narrative page was available to confirm intent.

findings.title: Snapshot fhir-type metadata for id.value changed from string to id

oldState.summary: R4 snapshot represents `id.value` as FHIRPath `System.String` and annotates the FHIR type extension as `string`; the R4 differential already annotates it as `id`.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 snapshot carries a computable annotation that can be read as the primitive value's FHIR type being `string`, even though the artifact itself is `id` and its differential says the fhir-type is `id`.

newState.summary: R6 snapshot and differential both represent `id.value` as FHIRPath `System.String` with fhir-type `id`; cardinality and regex are unchanged.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 snapshot aligns the fhir-type annotation with the datatype's canonical identity: `id` remains serialized as a primitive string value, but the metadata now names the primitive datatype rather than the base scalar.

facts.note: This is a computable metadata annotation in the snapshot, not a change to the FHIRPath scalar type.
The R4 and R6 differentials already agree.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The matched element has the same `id` and `path` (`id.value`) in both snapshots and differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a validation break: the primitive value remains a FHIRPath string with the same 1-to-64-character regex. The risk is limited to tools that generate primitive classes, validators, serializers, or schema metadata from the snapshot and compare or dispatch on the `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension. Such tools may now produce or expect a more specific `id` primitive type instead of treating the value as generic `string`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: No direct clinical or business safety risk was identified because accepted instance values and wire serialization are unchanged.

justification.inferredGoal: Align snapshot computable metadata with the `id` primitive datatype identity and with the differential.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: R6 could have kept the R4 snapshot `structuredefinition-fhir-type` marker as `string` while relying on the datatype identity, unchanged regex, differential, or supplemental metadata to identify `id` semantics.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 makes the snapshot value-type marker match the `id` primitive datatype and the R4/R6 differentials. The compatibility impact is low because R4-valid `id` instance values, cardinality, FHIRPath scalar type, regex, and wire format are unchanged; the breakage is limited to tooling that treated the R4 snapshot's inconsistent `string` marker as authoritative. Because the less-breaking path would preserve or duplicate a known metadata inconsistency, the correction is probably justified despite the tooling migration cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would have left `id.value`'s snapshot marker as `string` and required generators to infer the specialized primitive from `StructureDefinition.type = id`, the unchanged regex, the element path, the differential, or an added supplemental annotation. That is a real base-design alternative rather than ordinary migration guidance, but it is only partial: tools would have multiple sources of truth for the same primitive identity, the deprecated `string` marker might persist indefinitely, and the snapshot would still not cleanly express `id` as the authoritative FHIR primitive type.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would reduce churn for snapshot-only generators, but it would keep primary snapshot metadata inconsistent with the `id` datatype and create ambiguous primitive-typing signals for generic tooling.

evidence.detail: The R6 lexical regex remains `[A-Za-z0-9\-\.]{1,64}`, matching R4.

examples.examplesMd: No old-valid/new-invalid instance example is provided because the lexical value space is unchanged. A value such as `abc-123.4` remains valid in both R4 and R6, while a value longer than 64 characters remains invalid in both.

findings.narrativeMd: `id.value` keeps the same primitive wire representation and validation regex, but its R6 snapshot metadata now identifies the FHIR primitive type as `id` rather than `string`. Implementers most likely to notice are those with code generators or validators that consume snapshot type extensions directly. Data migration does not need to rewrite `id` values for this change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `id` instance does not become invalid solely because of this metadata change. Valid R6 `id` values remain representable in R4 because the regex, cardinality, and primitive string representation are unchanged. The compatibility issue is runtime/tooling-oriented: strict generated-code tests, schema snapshots, primitive-type registries, or serializer dispatch tables may need to account for `id` rather than `string` as the fhir-type annotation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review generators and validators that read `snapshot.element[].type[].extension` for primitive fhir-type metadata. Prefer the canonical StructureDefinition type and the local regex for validation, and add regression tests that confirm `id` values are still accepted as strings on the wire while preserving the specific primitive metadata where the R6 model expects `id`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably necessary to make the snapshot internally consistent with the `id` datatype and with the R4/R6 differentials. A backward-compatible alternative would have been to keep the R4 snapshot's `string` annotation, but that would continue to obscure the difference between the base scalar representation and the specialized FHIR primitive.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R4 and R6 use the same canonical URL, id, name, kind `primitive-type`, type `id`, baseDefinition `string`, specialization derivation, active status, and non-abstract flag.
Both snapshots contain the same local/inherited element paths: `id`, `id.id`, `id.extension`, and `id.value`. No local element was added, removed, renamed, split, merged, or moved.

The value remains represented as `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String`. The only type-related change is the snapshot fhir-type annotation correction covered by finding `id:SERIALIZATION_OR_CODEGEN:id.value:4b8c2f`.
The local regex is unchanged: `[A-Za-z0-9\-\.]{1,64}`. The 64-character length limit and permitted characters are therefore stable.

No local `id` invariant was added, removed, or strengthened in the differential. Constraint text and `xpath` differences visible in the snapshot are inherited from `Element` or `Extension` and are out of scope for this local report.
`id` has no terminology binding in either StructureDefinition.
`id` is a primitive datatype and has no reference target list in either version.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value was found for `id` or `id.value` in either version.
`isModifier` remains false for the snapshot elements where reported.
`isSummary` remains false for the snapshot elements where reported.
No slicing is present on `id` elements in either version.

The primitive value remains represented as an XML attribute (`xmlAttr`) and as the same primitive string value domain. The codegen metadata annotation change is tracked separately as a Low-impact finding.
Because R6 preserves the same lexical regex and cardinality for the primitive value, an R6 `id` value is representable in R4 without information loss at the `id` datatype level.

The local definition remains the same substance: allowed characters, length limit, examples of possible identifier forms, and case-insensitivity are unchanged. The top-level description prefix changed editorially from `Base StructureDefinition for id type` to `id type`; rendered narrative pages were not available.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds additional StructureDefinition metadata extensions
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds metadata such as `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` = `has-length`, `structuredefinition-wg` = `fhir`, `experimental=false`, jurisdiction, generated narrative text, and updated publisher/contact metadata. These do not change instance validity for `id`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata harvesters and documentation generators may see additional fields or extensions. FHIR consumers should tolerate unknown extensions and should not use exact metadata-field equality as a migration gate.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Top-level description prefix was editorially simplified
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 description begins `Base StructureDefinition for id type:` while R6 begins `id type:`. The substantive definition of allowed characters, length limit, examples, and case-insensitivity is unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation diff tools may flag the changed prefix, but validator behavior and datatype semantics should not change because of it.

`id.extension` exposes inherited `Extension` text and constraint representation differences, including `ext-1` `xpath` removal. These are excluded here and should be assessed in the `Extension` report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, change note, or issue reference was available to confirm the intended rationale for the snapshot fhir-type metadata change.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A published datatype diff or HL7 change note explaining the `id.value` snapshot annotation would confirm whether this is an intentional normalization or a generator artifact.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Rendered R4 and R6 datatype narrative pages were not consulted. The package StructureDefinitions provide the computable constraints, but rendered prose could clarify whether any additional semantic guidance changed.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare the rendered R4 `id` datatype page with the R6 ballot datatype page.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`) rather than a final publication; details may still change before a final R6 release.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run this assessment against the final R6 core package when it is published.
